answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require every agent to stake a small refundable bond tied to a verified work history before it may trade. To forge one identity is cheap, but to forge a thousand means locking a thousand bonds, so the cost grows linearly while honest agents pay once. A public reputation ledger acts like a lantern: past misbehavior stays visible, and one bad act sends a ripple through future trust scores, making fake fleets expensive to build and quick to expose.
